correctness.rationale: For n=2 the allocation is forced; for n=3 the score at fixed product R of the two failure probabilities is 3+R minus twice their sum, so equality is uniquely optimal. For n=4, independent enumeration by component sizes gives the six-pair score. At fixed middle failure probability v and fixed product uw, the only variable term is -(3-2v)(u+w); the strict AM–GM comparison gives the equality of the two outer allocations even when an endpoint is feasible. At equal outer failures u, outer success p=1-u, the middle marginal with respect to investment is v(2-u)^2; each outer marginal is u[1+(1-v)(2-u)]. Their difference is 2v(2-u)-u(3-u). Along the symmetric budget line v=R/u², the sign of the objective derivative with respect to u is the sign of R-H(u), H=u³(3-u)/[2(2-u)]. H is strictly increasing; H(sqrt R)<R since 2(2-u)-u(3-u)=(1-u)(4-u)>0 there, and H(1)=1>R. This proves the unique interior global optimum. The premium equals log(2(2-u)/(3-u)), strictly decreasing in u while u strictly decreases with B. Endpoint limits give 0 and log(4/3); H'(1)=7/2 and H(u) ~ 3u³/4 at zero yield both budget asymptotics. The exact benchmark R=5/48, u=1/2 has v=5/12 and score 37/16. This is an all-budget proof for independent equally priced exponential links, not a random-search inference.

value.rationale: The all-pairs score is a naturally used connectivity objective. In its smallest homogeneous path where link positions are not interchangeable, it is not enough to note that the middle marginal is larger at equality: the sharp result gives the interior global optimum and strict ordering for every budget, with an increasing but bounded log-effort premium. The exact budget dependence and transition from the three-patch symmetry case are useful baselines for continuous path investment. This is a model-level statement, not a species persistence or real restoration prediction.
